title: Scalar actions across an additive equivalence
statement: Let R be a ring, C and D preadditive categories, and e:C ≌ D an equivalence whose functor is additive. A scalar object is an object X equipped with a ring homomorphism R -> End(X); its morphisms commute with every scalar operation. Applying e to objects, morphisms and endomorphism ring actions induces an equivalence between scalar objects of C and D.

source.place: Tag 04JQ, lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point, scalar enhancement; Tag 04JM, lemma-global-sections-point

proof.text: Construct the scalar-object category using the commuting squares. An additive functor gives a ring homomorphism on endomorphisms and hence a functor on scalar objects. Full faithfulness of the original functor supplies preimages of scalar-compatible morphisms; apply faithfulness to their commuting-square equations.

source.place: Tag 04JQ, lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point, scalar enhancement; Tag 04JM, lemma-global-sections-point

proof.text: For a scalar object N of D, take X=e.inverse(N). Conjugate its R-action by the counit e(X) ≅ N, and pull that ring map back through the fully faithful endomorphism-ring equivalence. The counit and its inverse commute with the transported action. This proves essential surjectivity; together with full faithfulness it constructs the equivalence. The chosen inverse objects are determined up to scalar-compatible isomorphism by the already proved equivalence.
